claims.allowed_wording: A Boolean expression maps each complete assignment of its variables to one Boolean output.
claims.plain_wording: A Boolean rule turns each assignment into true or false.
claims.technical_wording: The expression classes evaluate a declared variable assignment to one Boolean value; enumerating assignments exposes the denoted Boolean function.

claims.allowed_wording: An expression is syntax; its Boolean function is the assignment-to-output mapping it denotes, so different expressions may denote the same function.
claims.plain_wording: The written rule and the function it computes are not the same object.
claims.technical_wording: Structural form is an expression property, while exact equality is established by matching outputs over the declared assignment universe.

claims.allowed_wording: An explicit CM is a dense truth-layout representation over a declared row/column variable split.
claims.plain_wording: A CM lays a Boolean function's truth values out as a matrix.
claims.technical_wording: The public dense output arranges assignments over row variables R and column variables C, with fixed values applied at evaluation.

claims.allowed_wording: Live support and ambient variables are distinct: live variables affect the function, while ambient variables may still define the displayed assignment universe.
claims.plain_wording: A function can depend on fewer variables than the table around it.
claims.technical_wording: Materialization tracks live variables after fixed bindings; an ambient layout may include axes absent from node.vars.

claims.allowed_wording: CM-IR is a canonicalized, interned shared DAG intermediate representation.
claims.plain_wording: CM-IR stores reusable computation structure, not a dense matrix.
claims.technical_wording: compile_expr_to_cm_ir builds canonical CMNode structures with interning, simplification, sharing-aware associative flattening, and optional persistent caching.

claims.allowed_wording: An explicit dense CM and CM-IR are different artifacts with different construction, storage, and evaluation boundaries.
claims.plain_wording: The matrix is an output layout; CM-IR is a reusable program graph.
claims.technical_wording: materialize_cm produces a dense array, whereas evaluate_compiled/materialize_hybrid_no_reinflate can return packed or flat truth output without dense CM reinflation.

claims.allowed_wording: CM, CM-IR, SAT, BDD, minimization, and symbolic algebra answer different questions and must be compared under matched output contracts.
claims.plain_wording: A truth layout, a reusable program, and a satisfying assignment are different outputs.
claims.technical_wording: Complete-vector extraction, point queries, restrictions, satisfiability, equivalence, minimization, and symbolic rewriting charge different work and cannot be ranked as one task.

claims.allowed_wording: CM-IR interns reusable nodes in a DAG and can retain roots that share descendants.
claims.plain_wording: Several outputs can point into one shared computation graph.
claims.technical_wording: CMNode identity and interning permit repeated structure to be stored once while compiled roots retain the requested outputs.

claims.technical_wording: Associative/commutative normalization and simplification affect canonical structure; structural digests identify it; intern tables reuse the resulting CMNode.
